Simultaneous Opposing Cardinal Directions has been added with “Last Input Priority” as the default. This means your most recent button press will take priority over any directions already pressed. SMITE 1 used a “Neutral” setting here where the inputs would cancel out. This can be adjusted in the Gameplay Settings

This is intended to convey the most basic concepts of the game, and more features will be implemented in the future to help players grow their skills over time as they learn the nuances of SMITE 2.
The role preference system has been reworked for SMITE 2.
Before queueing for a Conquest match, players will now order their preferred roles from 1 (most preferred) to 5 (least preferred), and roles for a team will be assigned based on these preferences
A player can also select “Fill” if they wish to rank all roles equally.

If a player does not receive one of their top 2 roles, they will be granted priority on role assignment for their next match. The amount of priority granted scales from “Priority” to “High Priority” based on a few factors. What earns a player priority are as follows (in order from most to least priority):
Being given their 3rd role, or playing a match with the “Fill” option

The first patch of the Ranked Test Season was successful at gathering the data we need in order to implement Ranked in the way we want in the long term, but we need to make some adjustments to the current format in order to maintain a healthy Ranked mode during the Alpha

Players will be able to queue for Ranked Conquest in a party of size 1, 2, or 5. Solo and Duo queues will be placed into the same matchmaking pool, and full parties will only be able to play other full parties

Dev note: Long term, we know what is needed to create a Solo and Party queue experience that follows our vision for SMITE 2 Ranked. However, for that to succeed, we have identified a few key systems we need to first develop to support that. During this point of the Alpha, the healthiest thing for Ranked is to combine the two most common forms of queueing (Solo and Duo) into one main queue for matchmaking and parity reasons, the option to play ranked in a Trio queue will return when those systems are developed.
Full Party (5 stack) queue times and matchmaking should be expected to be more variable, but this experience is something we still wanted to offer to players
Time to select a god has been reduced from 60s to 45s.

As we continue to work on matchmaking features, we have accelerated one system on our timeline in order to ensure there is healthy competition for top end players as we look towards building out SMITE 2’s competitive and esports scene, as well as a clear goal for non-established players to reach in order to start competing on a higher level
Elite Ranked Conquest is a separate Ranked queue which is unlocked after a player reaches Diamond Rank (3,200 SR)
The current threshold is likely lower than future versions, but established at this point so that Elite has a healthy player count during the Alpha.
A player will lose access to Elite Ranked after they fall below 2,600 SR
Elite Ranked Conquest is Solo Queue only
Once a player unlocks Elite Ranked Conquest (3,200 SR), they will earn and lose 50% less SR in any other Ranked queue
Once a player hits Master Rank (4,400 SR) they will earn and lose 90% less SR in any other Ranked queue
SR calculation post match has had a few small tweaks, as well as multiple bug fixes (resulting in both too much, or too little SR gained) that were addressed.
SR Party Reduction rules did not properly apply in the previous patch, allowing excessive SR gains (notably in parties of size 5) and that has also been fixed.

SR Reduction rules for Parties (size 2 and 5) have been updated so that SR differences are only counted past Bronze (800 SR), but past that point apply as 25/50/75% reduction for each 1200/1800/2400 SR difference in the party

If a player is affected by a Party SR Reduction (for playing in a party of a wide skill range) and a Solo SR Reduction (for playing outside Elite Ranked when qualified), the higher of the two values applies.
Players above Obsidian 2 Rank (4,000 SR) will be reset back to 4,000 SR.
In-Game leaderboards, displaying detailed information of the top 1000 players worldwide will be displayed from the Ranked Season page.
Currently, leaderboards will refresh periodically, with live leaderboards coming in a future update

If the Runic Bomb hits an enemy god, it instead deals 300 Physical damage and displaces them.
Enemies can attack the Runic Bomb to destroy it before it detonates.

After using Shining Metal Nu Wa gains Strength of Metal, which causes her Basic Attacks to hit all enemies within 2m of the target hit.
After using Fire Shards Nu Wa gains Strength of Fire, which causes her Basic Attacks to go farther and faster.

Nu Wa can stack any amount of Basic Attack modifiers. For example, if she has Strength of Metal, Strength of Fire, and Strength of Wood active all at once, her Basic Attack will go farther, faster, and Root all enemies hit within 2m of the target hit.
Every 15s your next Basic Attack will Root all targets hit. Damaging an enemy with a Basic Attack reduces this cooldown by 1s.
